\[ S_r = \sum_{n \ge 0} \binom{N}{n(p-1) + r} \]

\[ S_r \equiv \frac{1}{p-1} \sum_{x=1}^{p-1} x^{-r} (1+x)^N \pmod p \]
Since $p-1 \equiv -1 \pmod p$, this simplifies to:
\[ S_r \equiv - \sum_{x=1}^{p-1} x^{-r} (1+x)^N \pmod p \]
For $x \in \{1, \dots, p-2\}$, we have $1+x \in \mathbb{F}_p^*$, so $(1+x)^N \equiv (1+x)^{N \pmod{p-1}} \pmod p$. For $x = p-1 \equiv -1 \pmod p$, the term $(1+x)^N = 0^N = 0$ because $N \ge 1$.
Let $A = N \pmod{p-1}$. We calculate $A$ as follows:
\[ 10000 = 19 \times 502 + 462 \implies A = 462 \]
Thus, the sum becomes:
\[ S_r \equiv - \sum_{x=1}^{p-2} x^{-r} (1+x)^A \pmod p \]

\[ S_r \equiv - \sum_{z \in \mathbb{F}_p^*} z^{-r} \sum_{k=0}^A \binom{A}{k} z^k = - \sum_{k=0}^A \binom{A}{k} \sum_{z \in \mathbb{F}_p^*} z^{k-r} \pmod p \]
